newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Highest ever daily gain pushes BUX to high.
newsitem.headline: Highest ever daily gain pushes BUX to high.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange's record bull run continued on Thursday as the assessment of the country and of stocks kept on attracting large amounts of fresh capital to the market, traders said.
"Economic circumstances are favourable, results are growing, companies are good and the region is attractive," said Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securities.
"Fund managers have to spend their money and when buying stocks they are opening positions worth at least half a million dollars to a million dollars."
The BUX index soared to a fourth successive record of 5,126.39 points, up 201.14 points in the highest ever daily rise and in the second ever highest spot share turnover of 5.08 billion forints.
Investors' appetite for Hungarian stocks is bolstered by positive analyst comments on this market, Berecz said, referring to Merrill Lynch, released in a domestic newspaper.

The report said Hungarian shares offered the most attractive price/earnings ratio this year and the analysis predicted that even more capital will flow into east European stocks due to sinking inflation rates.
Bank stocks outpaced most other stocks benefiting from a bullish note on the market.
"So far they have not risen at the same pace as other stocks and now they want to catch up with them," one trader said earlier today.
OTP surged to a new record level of 4,000 forints, up 550 forints or 15.94 percent. Inter-Europa Bank put on 10 percent or 3,900 forints to finish at 44,500, also a new high.
A number of stocks joined the group of record breakers, including hotelier Danubius which soared to 5,005 forints, up 545; the chemicals and all the three pharmaceuticals stocks.

On the losing side stood the Global Depositary Receipts of Cofinec following the announcement of the merger of its two Hungarian units to improve productivity and to reduce costs. Cofinec finished at 5,350 forints, down 110.
Losers also included oil and gas company MOL which lost 75 forints to finish 2,650 forints.

Traders said one likely reason behind MOL's fall was its expected selloff ahead of which many investors might have decided to sell with the aim of profit-taking on hopes to buy the shares back at a lower price.
Traders said they saw increasing danger of panic sales by domestic investors once the market's rise stops.
"Domestic investors entering the rally in its late phase, will react to the falter with panic sales," Berecz said.
